procedure.description: inpatient admission, septicemia or severe sepsis without mechanical ventilation over 96 hours, with major complication or comorbidity

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for MS-DRG 871 (inpatient admission, septicemia or severe sepsis without mechanical ventilation over 96 hours, with major complication or comorbidity) with dates of service 2026-04-18 through 2026-04-19. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. RARC N10: Adjustment based on the findings of a review organization. Payer remark: Inpatient level of care is not supported by the clinical documentation. Observation services were appropriate for the services rendered; the claim is denied as billed.

criteria.text: Sepsis documented by a suspected or confirmed infection with at least two systemic inflammatory response criteria or a qSOFA score of 2 or more, together with evidence of hypoperfusion or organ dysfunction such as a lactate of 2 or more or hypotension.
Treatment required inpatient-level resources: intravenous fluid resuscitation of 30 mL/kg, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, serial lactate measurement, and continuous hemodynamic monitoring.

At the time of the admission order, the admitting physician documented a reasonable expectation that care would span at least two midnights, and the actual stay met that expectation or was shortened by an unforeseen event.
The condition could not be safely treated with outpatient or observation services.

chart.text: 61 year old woman brought in by her spouse with two days of fever, chills, and left-sided back pain, poor oral intake since yesterday. History of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. On arrival temperature 39.2, heart rate 118, respiratory rate 24, blood pressure 86 over 50, oxygen saturation 94 percent on room air. Looks sick. Left flank tenderness, urine cloudy. Working diagnosis pyelonephritis with sepsis.

Admission history and physical. Assessment: pyelonephritis. Plan as above. Family updated at the bedside. 2.75 liters of lactated Ringer’s given as a 30 per kilo bolus in the department, piperacillin-tazobactam started within the hour. Repeat lactate every 6 hours until cleared, telemetry, strict intake and output, hold the lisinopril. Admit inpatient for now. She will likely be able to go home tomorrow if she responds to fluids and the repeat lactate is down.
Lactate 3.1. White count 19.2 with 12 percent bands. Creatinine 1.8, baseline 1.0 from last year. Urinalysis: many white cells, nitrite positive. Blood and urine cultures sent.
Dentures labeled and placed in the denture cup at the bedside. Patient prefers them out at night. Oral care done.
Home atorvastatin resumed at the home dose this morning after review with the attending. No interactions flagged.
Audiology screen at nursing's request. She wears a hearing aid on the right, battery replaced, hears conversational voice well now. No further needs.
Potassium 3.2 this morning, repleted with 40 milliequivalents oral per protocol. Recheck with morning labs.
Chaplain visited at the patient's request, about twenty minutes. She appreciated the visit. No needs identified.
Overnight: vital signs every 2 hours, two episodes of rigors, warm blankets, acetaminophen given. Tolerating sips. Urine output recorded hourly.

Hospital day 2, morning. Responded to the first liter; blood pressure held overnight without more fluid, heart rate 88, afebrile since midnight. Repeat lactate 1.4. Creatinine 1.3. Switch to oral antibiotics and discharge today with a culture callback.

Discharged the next morning, under 24 hours after arrival. Lactate normalized to 1.4 after the first liter, blood pressure 118 over 72 overnight without further fluid, afebrile. Home on oral antibiotics with a culture callback.
Fall risk assessment completed, score 53, high risk. Bed alarm on, nonskid socks, call light within reach, hourly rounding. Family at bedside this evening.
Skin assessment on admission. Braden 14. Skin intact, no pressure injury, heels floated. Turn every two hours while in bed. Barrier cream to the sacrum as a precaution.
Dietitian consult. Regular diet with heart healthy modification. Intake about 69 percent of meals. Supplement shake twice daily added. Will follow.
IV site rotated from the left forearm to the right hand, old site without redness. Dressing dated. Patient tolerated well.
Glucose checks before meals and at bedtime, ranging 149 to 221. Sliding scale given per protocol. Patient's own glucometer at bedside, sent home with family for safekeeping.
Daily weight 160 pounds, up 1 from yesterday. Intake and output recorded. Repositioned per schedule, skin checked.
Patient requested something for sleep. Melatonin 3 milligrams given per order at 2130. Slept in two-hour stretches per night shift report.
Bowel regimen started, senna and docusate at bedtime. Last bowel movement 2 days ago per patient. Encouraged fluids and ambulation as able.
Pharmacy note. Renal dosing reviewed, creatinine 0.9, no adjustments needed today. Home medication list reconciled with the daughter by phone, one duplicate statin removed.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-3 (twoMidnights) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan, a shortfall, or a result below the threshold.
